fi-mikrogeophagus-ramirezi.title: German Blue Ram (incl. Electric Blue, Gold and Balloon strains)
fi-mikrogeophagus-ramirezi.summary: A small, jewel-colored dwarf cichlid that needs warm, soft, very clean water.
rows: About 1.6 in (4 cm) body length. Males are larger
24 × 12 in footprint (about 15 gal) or larger for one pair
Peaceful, but pairs defend a territory about 2 ft across when breeding
Keep singly or as a pair. Calm schooling fish nearby make it less shy
Sifts the substrate for food. Live or frozen bloodworm, brine shrimp and daphnia plus small sinking pellets
Moderate. Needs stable, clean water and isn't a good fit for a general community tank
notes: Never add to a new tank. Use gentle flow and small regular water changes (10–15%).
Good tankmates are peaceful fish that also like the heat, such as cardinal tetras. Avoid other cichlids and boisterous fish.
Fancy strains like gold, long-fin and balloon tend to be weaker and shorter-lived than wild-type fish.
warn: Needs warmer water (81–86°F) than most community fish.

fi-nannacara-anomala.title: Golden Dwarf Cichlid
fi-nannacara-anomala.summary: The golden dwarf cichlid, Nannacara anomala, ranges from the Rio Aruka in Guyana to the lower Rio Marowijne in Suriname. It is often found in flooded grassland in low-lying coastal areas, but most…
rows: Carnivore / micropredator. It's naturally a micropredator , foraging for worms, insects and other invertebrates in the wild.
The natural range of this species extends from the Rio Aruka in Guyana to the lower Rio Marowijne in Suriname .
notes: Provide a well planted setup with bits of bogwood , driftwood or mopani wood to provide cover and spawning sites for these fish.

fi-satanoperca-jurupari.title: Jurupari Eartheater
fi-satanoperca-jurupari.summary: The demon eartheater, Satanoperca jurupari, is a cichlid recorded throughout much of the Amazon basin in Brazil, Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia. In aquarium literature it is frequently confused…
rows: Recorded throughout much of the Amazon river basin in Brazil, Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador, and Colombia (and possibly the Orinoco watershed in Colombia and Venezuela; see 'Notes'), but…
notes: The most essential item of décor is a soft, sandy substrate so that the fish can browse naturally (see 'Diet').
Coarser materials such as gravel or small pebbles can inhibit feeding, damage gill filaments and even be ingested with the potential of internal damage or blockages.

fi-aequidens-pulcher.title: Aequidens pulcher
fi-aequidens-pulcher.summary: The blue acara, Andinoacara pulcher, is a cichlid native to Trinidad and Tobago and parts of Venezuela. It occupies a variety of habitats, from murky still waters to clear streams. A mainstay of the…
rows: Mainly carnivorous , so offer meaty fare such as bloodoworm, brine shrimp , chopped mussel or prawn and earthworms.
Native to Trinidad and Tobago plus parts of Venezuela , and has been introduced in various other countries.
notes: The tank should ideally be furnished with a soft, sandy substrate and driftwood branches.
Floating plants to provide shade are also a good idea, but rooted plants are less so, as this fish is an avid digger.

fi-heros-severus.title: Heros severus
fi-heros-severus.summary: The severum, Heros efasciatus, is a cichlid from the Amazon main channel and the Rio Solimoes, also recorded from the Rio Xingu. One of the most popular and readily available cichlids in the hobby,…
rows: Widespread throughout the Amazon main channel and rio Solimoes and also recorded from the rio Xingu .
notes: A biotope setup would be very simple to arrange.

Use a substrate of river sand and add a few driftwood branches (if you can't find driftwood of the desired shape, common beech is safe to use if thoroughly dried and stripped of bark) and twisted roots.

fi-rocio-octofasciata.title: Rocio octofasciata
fi-rocio-octofasciata.summary: The Jack Dempsey cichlid, Rocio octofasciata, is native to the Atlantic slope of Central America in Mexico, Belize, Guatemala and Honduras. Its name apparently comes from the American heavyweight…
rows: Pairs or small groups depending on setup
Omnivore. Wild specimens are likely omnivorous but with a preference for aquatic invertebrates and suchlike.
Native to the Atlantic slope of Central America in Mexico, Belize , Guatemala, and Honduras with its known range extending southwards from the Río Actopan in Veracruz state,…
notes: Ideally a soft, sandy substrate should be used though it’s not essential, and one or two flattish, water-worn rocks can also be included to provide potential spawning sites.

Additional furnishings are as much a case of personal taste as anything else but the most favoured set-ups tend to feature relatively dim lighting plus some chunks of driftwood and scattered roots or branches.

fi-amphilophus-labiatus.title: Amphilophus labiatus
fi-amphilophus-labiatus.summary: The red devil cichlid, Amphilophus labiatus, is a large cichlid endemic to Lakes Nicaragua and Managua in Nicaragua, living near submerged rocks. It is often confused with the midas cichlid, A.…
rows: One of the least fussy feeders you are likely to encounter in the hobby, most specimens will attempt to eat anything that looks as though it might be edible.
Endemic to the Lakes of Nicaragua and Managua in Nicaragua, Central America.
notes: There are few fish that show less regard for a beautifuly decorated tank than this species.
Don't even consider a planted setup, as large quantities of the substrate will be shifted around on a daily basis.

fi-thorichthys-meeki.title: Firemouth Meeki Cichlid
fi-thorichthys-meeki.summary: The firemouth cichlid, Thorichthys meeki, is a Central American cichlid from Mexico's Atlantic slope and the Yucatán south into Belize and Guatemala. A popular aquarium fish for a long time, it is…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates

Predator / carnivore. Thorichthys species are primarily benthophagous omnivores with wild individuals often feeding on small crustaceans such as copepods and cladocerans, plus other invertebrates, molluscs , and organic detritus.
Its natural range extends eastward from the Río Tonalá system near Coatzacoalcos, on Mexico 's Atlantic slope, through the states of Veracruz, Chiapas, Tabasco, around the Yucatán…
notes: Provided adequate cover and structure is available this species is unfussy with regards to décor with ceramic flowerpots, lengths of plastic piping and other artificial materials all useful additions.

A more natural-looking arrangement might consist of a soft, sandy substrate with smooth rocks plus some driftwood roots and branches placed in such a way that plenty of shady spots and caves are formed.

fi-andinoacara-rivulatus.title: Green Terror Cichlid
fi-andinoacara-rivulatus.summary: The green terror cichlid, Andinoacara rivulatus, is a large cichlid from extreme northern Peru and the coastal drainages of western Ecuador. Generally aggressive and territorial, it is best kept…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates
Usually kept singly (or a known pair when breeding)
Native to extreme northern Peru and coastal drainages of western Ecuador as far north as the Río Esmeraldas drainage and possibly beyond.
notes: The tank should ideally be furnished with a soft, sandy substrate and driftwood branches, with some large flat rocks to act as potential spawning sites.
If there are other fish in the tank, arrange the decor to provide as many visual barriers as possible.

fi-cleithracara-maronii.title: Keyhole Cichlid
fi-cleithracara-maronii.summary: The keyhole cichlid, Cleithracara maronii, is a small cichlid from French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, the Orinoco delta in Venezuela and Trinidad. It is told apart from relatives by the keyhole-shaped…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates
Schooling / social — keep a proper group
Predator / carnivore. Likely to be a foraging omnivore feeding on benthic invertebrates and organic detritus in nature.
Described from the Maroni in French Guiana and occurs in most river drainages of the country as well as Guyana , Suriname , the Orinoco delta region in Venezuela and island of…
notes: Provided adequate cover and structure is available this species is unfussy with regards to décor with ceramic flowerpots, lengths of plastic piping and other artificial materials all useful additions.
Since it tends not to dig it can also be maintained in most planted aquaria.

fi-crenicichla-compressiceps.title: Green Yellow Tail Dwarf Pike Cichlid
fi-crenicichla-compressiceps.summary: The compressiceps dwarf pike cichlid, Wallaciia compressiceps, is a small pike cichlid known only from the lower Rio Tocantins basin in Brazil. It swims a great deal and can be very quick and very…
rows: Tank bred specimens will happily take most foods, but wild caught fish may demand live or at the least frozen foods.
Known only from the lower Rio Tocantins basin , Brazil .
notes: Provide an aquarium with plenty of hiding places, especially using bits of wood and leaves scattered across the substrate.
Plants are fine, it is unlikely that Compressiceps will unearth them.

fi-geophagus-brasiliensis.title: Geophagus Brasiliensis Cichlid
fi-geophagus-brasiliensis.summary: The pearl cichlid, Geophagus brasiliensis, comes from Atlantic-draining river systems of eastern and southern Brazil and Uruguay. It belongs to the 'G.' brasiliensis group, which still needs…
rows: Predator / carnivore. Studies have revealed it to be a generalised omnivore with the natural diet composed of plant material, aquatic invertebrates (particularly chironomid larvae, ostracods and cladocerans), fish scales and fry.
Native to river systems of eastern and southern Brazil and Uruguay draining into the Atlantic Ocean with type locality given as 'Rio de Janeiro Bay, Brazil'.
notes: Ideally a soft, sandy substrate should be employed though it's not essential.

Additional furnishings are as much a case of personal taste as anything else but the most favoured set-ups tend to feature relatively dim lighting plus some chunks of driftwood and scattered roots or branches.

fi-geophagus-steindachneri.title: Red Hump Geo. Steindachneri Cichlid
fi-geophagus-steindachneri.summary: The red hump eartheater, Geophagus steindachneri, is a cichlid from the Magdalena and Sinú drainages in Colombia and the Río Limón basin in Venezuela. It lends its name to the 'G.' steindachneri…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates
Usually kept singly (or a known pair when breeding)

Herbivore / algae browser. Benthophagous by nature, mostly employing a feeding strategy whereby mouthfuls of substrate are taken and sifted for edible items with the remaining material expelled via the gills and mouth.
Widespread throughout the Río Magdalena drainage, Colombia , including its major tributary the Río Cauca, plus the Río Sinú drainage in northwestern Colombia and Río Limón basin,…
notes: The most essential item of décor is a soft, sandy substrate so that the fish can browse naturally (see 'Diet').
Coarser materials such as gravel or small pebbles can inhibit feeding, damage gill filaments and even be ingested with the potential of internal damage or blockages.

fi-gymnogeophagus-balzanii.title: Geophagus Balzanii Cichlid
fi-gymnogeophagus-balzanii.summary: The Paraguay eartheater, Gymnogeophagus balzanii, is a cichlid from the Rio Paraná basin in Brazil, Paraguay and Argentina, and the Rio Uruguay. It is found away from the main river channels in…
rows: Schooling / social — keep a proper group
Herbivore / algae browser. Easily fed, provided anything offered sinks, as it will rarely feed from anywhere other than the substrate.
Various drainages of the Rio Paraná basin in Brazil , Paraguay and Argentina .
notes: A biotope setup would consist very simply of a sandy substrate, perhaps with some driftwood branches and twisted roots added for effect.
Aquatic plants are not a feature of the species' natural habitat, and would doubtless be uprooted by its sand-sifting activity anyway.

fi-herichthys-carpintis.title: Green Texas/Carpintis Cichlid
fi-herichthys-carpintis.summary: The pearlscale cichlid, Herichthys carpintis, is a large cichlid from northern Mexico, found in lagoons around the mouth of the Panuco drainage. It is often mislabelled as the Texas or green Texas…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates
notes: As long as territories (rock, wood) and open space is provided in the aquarium, Carpintis aren't too fussed.
Plants rooted in the substrate will likely be uprooted as the Pearlscale Cichlid is a digger.

fi-hypselecara-temporalis.title: Chocolate Cichlid
fi-hypselecara-temporalis.summary: The chocolate cichlid, Hypselecara temporalis, is a large cichlid from Peru, Colombia, Venezuela and Brazil. It most often inhabits silt-laden, slow-flowing rivers, and has been collected in the…
rows: Omnivore. It's omnivorous , feeding on a variety of invertebrates, algae and other plant matter in the wild.
Widely distributed in parts of Peru , Colombia , Venezuela and Brazil .
notes: A sand substrate is preferable, with large pieces of bogwood and smooth boulders as additional decor.
Plants can be used if you wish, as it doesn't usually dig.

fi-hypsophrys-nicaraguensis.title: Nicaraguense Cichlid
fi-hypsophrys-nicaraguensis.summary: The Nicaragua cichlid, Hypsophrys nicaraguensis, is a Central American cichlid from Nicaragua and Costa Rica, found in lakes and slow-moving rivers. Also known as the spilotum or moga, it exists in…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates
Pairs or small groups depending on setup
Omnivore. Will accept most things offered.
notes: Provide plenty of cover in the form of rocks and other decor, such as bogwood or large flowerpots.
These should be arranged in such a way as to form caves and hiding places.

fi-mikrogeophagus-altispinosus.title: Bolivian Ram
fi-mikrogeophagus-altispinosus.summary: The Bolivian ram, Mikrogeophagus altispinosus, is a cichlid endemic to the upper rio Madeira basin in Bolivia and Brazil. Also traded as 'hi-fin ram' and 'Bolivian butterfly', it is larger and less…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates
group of 6-8 or more provided the aquarium is spacious ( 120 cm 47 in length or larger).
This species is considered endemic to the upper rio Madeira basin in Bolivia and Brazil.
notes: The most essential addition is a soft, sandy substrate so that the fish can browse naturally (see 'Diet').
Coarser options such as gravel or small pebbles can inhibit feeding, damage gill filaments and even be ingested with the potential of internal damage or blockages.

fi-amatitlania-nigrofasciata.title: Convict Cichlid
fi-amatitlania-nigrofasciata.summary: The convict cichlid, Amatitlania nigrofasciata, is a Central American cichlid native from Guatemala to Panama. One of the most ubiquitous fish in the hobby, it is hardy and very easily bred, but…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates
Very unfussy and will accept most foods offered.
Has a widespread distribution in Central America, being native to Guatemala, Honduras , El Salvador , Nicaragua , Costa Rica and Panama .
notes: Use rocks, bogwood and roots to provide plenty of hiding places and potential spawning sites for the fish.
You may also wish to provide additional caves in the form of suitably sized clay flower pots laid on their side.
